lead_story.topic: White Sox blow 4.5-game AL Central lead in 17 days—Chicago's historic collapse fueled by worst offense in baseball and absurd Tommy Pham elevator story
lead_story.headline: White Sox historic collapse: blow 4.5-game lead, now OUT of first place after 3-14 stretch—Tommy Pham only playing today because he ran into GM in elevator

tweets.text:

lead_story.research_notes: LEAD ANGLE: The White Sox have completed one of the most spectacular late-season collapses in recent AL Central history. On Aug. 30 they held a 4.5-game lead. Seventeen days later they are OUT of first place after going 3-14. The collapse is fueled by historically bad hitting: among 167 players with 50+ PA since Aug. 30, the three WORST hitters in baseball ALL play for Chicago (Colson Montgomery 165/167, Braden Montgomery 166/167, Munetaka Murakami 167/167). And the absurdity peaked today when Tommy Pham—who only got into the game because he ran into GM Chris Getz in an ELEVATOR last night and told him he was good to return from injury—hit a 3-run HR in his first game back. You can't make this up. HISTORICAL CONTEXT: Research past AL Central collapses. How does a 4.5-game lead evaporating in 17 days rank? What about the hitting futility—has any team ever had the three worst hitters in baseball over a 2-3 week stretch? MEME ANGLE: The elevator story is peak White Sox dysfunction. The fact that Pham had to lobby the GM in an elevator just to get activated, then immediately homered, encapsulates the chaos. GIF CONCEPT: weary resignation as the season slips away—the White Sox faithful watching their team blow a division lead in real time.
